title: Cache Telemetry Rollout Plan (staging → canary → prod)
content:
Owner: Connor O’Brien (Release / canary coordination)
Last updated: 2025-03-12

Purpose
Enable the new prefix/KV cache telemetry (hit/miss, miss-reason taxonomy, evictions/pressure, wasted prefill, reuse histograms) across environments with:
- near-zero runtime overhead
- controlled metric cardinality/cost
- clear dashboards + runbook for triage
- safe rollback that doesn’t require immediate code revert

This plan covers: staging → perf canary → limited prod canary → gradual prod rollout.

What is being rolled out (high-level)
1) Runtime instrumentation + config flags
- KV cache hit/miss counters + miss reasons
- Prefix cache reuse histograms / reuse depth
- Eviction counts + memory pressure gauges
- Wasted prefill metric
- Trace span annotations for cache events (low-cardinality)
- Local sampling + rate-limits (to bound overhead)

2) Context tagging / join keys
- Route + model version propagation into runtime metrics (allowlisted)
- Deployment mode + region tags

3) Ingestion-side guards
- Cardinality controls + label allowlists
- Drop/aggregate forbidden label combinations

4) Dashboards + alerts
- Initial panels shipped with conservative thresholds
- Alerts staged: “notify-only” first, then paging/ticketing after baseline is established

Definitions / feature flags (names are conceptual; exact config keys in runtime docs)
- cache_telemetry.enabled (bool)
- cache_telemetry.sample_rate (0.0–1.0)
- cache_telemetry.event_rate_limit_per_sec (int)
- cache_telemetry.allow_route_tag (bool, enforced by allowlist)
- cache_telemetry.allow_model_version_tag (bool, enforced by allowlist)
- cache_telemetry.trace_annotations.enabled (bool)

Default proposal by environment (can be tuned after canary)
- staging: enabled=true, sample_rate=1.0
- perf-canary: enabled=true, sample_rate=1.0
- prod canary: enabled=true, sample_rate=0.10 (10%), trace_annotations.enabled=true
- prod general: enabled=true, sample_rate=0.02–0.05, trace_annotations.enabled=true

Rollout timeline (target)
- D0 (Thu 2025-03-06): staging enablement + initial data quality validation
- D1 (Fri): perf-canary run + overhead gating
- D2 (Mon): prod canary (1 region, small slice) + ingestion/cardinality verification
- D3–D5: expand to 25% → 50% → 100% (or hold if baselines are still settling)

Pre-rollout prerequisites (must be done before enabling in any env)
[Runtime]
- Code merged: instrumentation + sampling/rate-limits + double-counting fixes
- Integration test merged for cache hit/miss + batched prefill semantics
- Config flags wired per environment (no hardcoded “always on”)

[Platform/Gateway tagging]
- Route_id + model_id/model_version_id propagation shipped
- Allowlist config checked for route/model/version labels (avoid per-tenant explosion)

[Telemetry ingestion]
- Cardinality guardrails deployed (drop/aggregate rules live)
- Budget estimate reviewed (series count OK at target sample_rate)

[Observability]
- Dashboards deployed (at least to internal ops folder)
- Alerts created but initially disabled OR set to notify-only
- Runbook link available from dashboard

[Security/Privacy]
- Confirm: no raw prompts, no unhashed prompt identifiers, only bucketed prompt-length/token metrics


Gate criteria summary (used at each stage)
A) Runtime overhead (perf)
- p95 latency regression: ≤ 1.0% on perf-canary workload
- p99 latency regression: ≤ 2.0% on perf-canary workload
- GPU utilization change: no sustained >2–3% increase attributable to telemetry
- No meaningful increase in error rate / retries

B) Telemetry correctness + consistency
- Non-zero signal where expected (hit/miss counters increment on repeat prompts)
- No double counting on streaming retries (validated via regression test + spot-check)
- Batched prefill attribution is sane (no impossible hit-rates >100%, no negative deltas)
- Miss-reason taxonomy populated and stable (no “unknown” dominating unless expected)

C) Cardinality + cost
- Series counts within budget (no route explosion)
- Drops due to guardrails are within expected bounds and visible (i.e., we can distinguish “drop” vs “no traffic”)
- No ingestion lag/backpressure spikes from cache metrics

D) Dashboards + alert readiness
- Primary dashboard renders within normal latency; panels are correctly filtered by region/model/deployment mode
- Baseline established for hit-rate + wasted prefill in at least one region/model


Stage 1: Staging rollout
Owner(s): Omar (runtime), Caleb (ingestion), Allison (dashboards)

Steps
1. Deploy runtime build to staging with cache_telemetry.enabled=true, sample_rate=1.0
2. Enable route/model tags in staging only (confirm allowlist in place)
3. Send a known repeated-prompt workload through staging (script or manual)
4. Validate in dashboards:
   - KV hit/miss counters increment
   - prefix reuse histogram has entries
   - eviction/pressure gauges show reasonable values
   - wasted_prefill >0 only when expected
5. Validate ingestion guards:
   - check “dropped_series_count” (or equivalent) panel/log
   - confirm no unexpected label values (route/model_version)

Gates to move to perf-canary
- Correctness checks pass (no obvious counting bugs)
- No staging runtime instability attributed to telemetry

Rollback (staging)
- Flip cache_telemetry.enabled=false in staging config
- If ingestion guard misconfig is causing drops/noise: tighten allowlist / disable route tags, keep core metrics only


Stage 2: Perf-canary rollout (dedicated perf validation)
Owner: Marcus Reed

Goal
Quantify overhead on representative workloads and fail fast if telemetry introduces latency regressions.

Steps
1. Run perf-canary with telemetry enabled at sample_rate=1.0
2. Collect before/after comparisons:
   - p50/p95/p99 latency
   - tokens/sec
   - CPU overhead (if applicable)
   - memory footprint deltas
3. If regression near threshold, rerun with lower sample_rate (0.25, 0.10) to calibrate prod default.

Gates to move to prod canary
- Meets overhead gate criteria (see above)
- No new tail spikes correlated with trace annotation emission

Rollback (perf-canary)
- Stop rollout; open ENG ticket against runtime instrumentation and revert/patch
- If only trace annotations are problematic: disable cache_telemetry.trace_annotations.enabled for prod canary


Stage 3: Production canary (limited scope)
Owner(s): Connor (coordination), Logan (pipelines), Allison (dashboards)

Scope proposal
- 1 region (start with us-east)
- 1–5% of fleet or a small subset of routes (prefer internal/test + a low-risk hosted segment)
- sample_rate=0.10, event_rate_limit enabled

Steps
1. Deploy runtime to prod canary pool with telemetry enabled (do NOT change global default yet)
2. Confirm ingestion guards are active in prod (observability-pack/pr-613 equivalent deployed)
3. Confirm dashboards show canary pool data (filter by pool/region)
4. Monitor for 2–4 hours minimum (include a traffic peak if possible):
   - p95/p99 latency
   - error rate, retry rate
   - ingestion lag/backpressure
   - metric drop counters
   - series cardinality
5. Sanity check “joinability”
   - route_id present
   - model_version_id consistent with gateway/control plane

Gates to expand
- Overhead within thresholds in live conditions
- No cardinality blowups; dropped metrics are within expected bounds and not masking all data
- Dashboards usable for triage; at least one “real” cache behavior insight visible (e.g., miss reasons split)

Rollback (prod canary)
Primary rollback (fast, no redeploy)
- Flip cache_telemetry.enabled=false for canary pool
Secondary rollback
- Reduce sample_rate to 0.01
- Disable route/model_version tags (keep only model family + region)
- Disable trace annotations if traces are too heavy
Tertiary rollback
- Remove canary build from pool / roll back runtime deployment

Escalation triggers during canary (stop + rollback)
- p95 latency regression > 1% sustained for 30 min (after controlling for traffic mix)
- Any p99 regression > 2% sustained for 15 min
- Ingestion lag or metric drop > agreed threshold (coordinate with Logan/Caleb)
- Unexpected metric explosion: new label values increasing series count rapidly


Stage 4: Gradual production rollout
Owner: Connor

Expansion plan (default)
- 25% of prod (same regions) for 24h
- 50% for 24h
- 100% after 48–72h stable

Operational notes
- Keep sample_rate conservative at first; we can increase later once we understand costs.
- Alerts should stay notify-only until we have at least ~1 week of baseline (diurnal patterns + workload mix variance).

Gates at each expansion step
- Overhead within thresholds
- No new ingest incidents; cardinality stable
- Data quality stable (no sudden “all zeros” panels indicating drop/mismatch)

Rollback (gradual rollout)
- Halt expansion, revert to previous percentage
- If issue is scoped to specific region/model: disable telemetry only for that region/model allowlist entry


Checklist (copy/paste for go/no-go meeting)
Preflight
[ ] Runtime build promoted to staging
[ ] Staging validation complete (metrics increment, sane values)
[ ] perf-canary run complete and within overhead thresholds
[ ] Ingestion cardinality guardrails deployed to prod
[ ] Dashboards deployed + accessible (SRE + Runtime)
[ ] Runbook link present from dashboard
[ ] Feature flags present and configurable per pool

Prod canary go/no-go
[ ] Canary scope agreed (region, % fleet, route subset)
[ ] sample_rate and rate-limit set
[ ] Owners on point for monitoring window (Runtime + Telemetry + SRE)
[ ] Rollback mechanism tested (config flip)

Expand to 25/50/100%
[ ] Canary stable for minimum monitoring window
[ ] No unexplained series blowups
[ ] No sustained p95/p99 regressions
[ ] Metrics are joinable by route/model_version
[ ] Communication sent (eng-oncall + #eng-runtime + #eng-sre)


Comms plan
- Announce rollout start + canary scope in #eng-oncall and #eng-releases
- Post dashboard links and the rollback switch location
- If rollback triggered, post a short incident note + next steps and file a follow-up ticket

Open questions / TODO
- Confirm exact prod default sample_rate after perf-canary results (Marcus to recommend)
- Decide whether to enable trace annotations by default in prod or only in canary first
- Finalize “notify-only” alert routing + thresholds after 1 week baseline

Sign-offs (informal)
- Runtime: Omar El-Sayed
- Telemetry pipelines: Logan Wright / Caleb Johnson
- SRE/observability: Allison Grant / Sean Gallagher
- Release coordinator: Connor O’Brien
